figures.title: Speech-intention decoding in 13 components: what the ledger records
figures.subtitle: Share of ledger entries with at least one fact for each component: silent speech, brain-to-text and lip reading
figures.note: 8,995 ledger entries, not yet deduplicated or scope-filtered. △ notes how to read a low share.
figures.caption: Every speech-intention decoder, whatever its sensor, can be described by the same 13 components: what the user does in training and in use, what is sensed, how it is decoded, what comes out, how the user confirms or corrects it, and how it is evaluated. Shares measure what the maintainer's normalized ledger (spec v2.1) has recorded. Runtime aids (M07) are under-recorded: of 3,245 decoding papers, 78 have M07 recorded, while about 440 mention a language model, beam search or lexicon in their methods and roughly half of those use one. Confirmation (M09) and correction (M10) are genuinely rare: 65 papers describe them (17 more ledger entries state "none"), and a full-text check found only a dozen or so missed, mostly text-entry BCIs and input systems.
